newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian combat troops complete Chechnya pullout.
newsitem.headline: Russian combat troops complete Chechnya pullout.

text.p: The last Russian combat unit withdrew from Chechnya on Sunday under a peace deal between Moscow and separatist leaders, Itar-Tass news agency said.
It quoted Russia's security chief Ivan Rybkin as saying that only logistics and transport units would remain in Chechnya pending a final pullout next month.
Rybkin, who is President Boris Yeltsin's personal envoy to Chechnya and secretary of his policy-making Security Council, did not specify which combat unit was the last to leave Chechnya.
Under the peace deal signed on August 31 Moscow promised to withdraw its forces, which were sent to Chechnya in December 1994 to quell the southern region's independence bid.

The rebels, for their part, agreed to postpone by five years the decision on Chechnya's political status. But their leaders make little secret that they still want full independence. Tens of thousands of people have died in 21 months of fighting.
The separatist leadership has called local elections for January 27 to elect a Chechen president and parliament. They are pressing Moscow to complete the pullout by the day of polls.
